1.e4 e6 2.d3 d5 3.Nd2.strategy: Keeps the d-file blocked, so that ...dxe4 does not force an exchange of queens as it would after Nf3. White chooses a slow, solid set-up: pieces behind the pawn on e4, and the plan of building a kingside attack from there with a later e-pawn advance.

1.e4 e6 2.d3 d5 3.Nd2 Nf6.strategy: Develops and attacks e4 a second time, so White must keep the pawn protected rather than push ahead. Black commits to a classical set-up and still has a choice of how to challenge White's centre.
